reason: FAQ risk answer states you are responsible for availability of the XKS Proxy and external key material, and that an unavailable proxy or key manager makes the EC2 instance with an XKS-encrypted EBS volume fail to launch.
Quotes state XKS keys can be used from your own applications with client-side symmetric encryption using KMS as key provider, and name the Encryption SDK, S3 and DynamoDB Encryption Clients.
Quotes define XKS as a custom key store backed by infrastructure you own and manage outside AWS, with all encrypt/decrypt operations performed in your key manager.
Quotes describe the data key encrypted first by a key in AWS KMS then a second time in the external key manager, and that no ciphertext can ever be decrypted without the external key material.
Quotes state you are solely responsible for durability of external keys and that permanent loss or deletion makes all ciphertext under the XKS key unrecoverable.
Quotes exclude XKS from the public KMS availability SLA and exclude XKS keys from the availability SLA of any service where you configure them.
Quotes give $1 per month per key until deleted, like all customer managed keys, and requests charged at the same rate as other symmetric KMS keys.
Quotes state a single request including one retry over 500ms returns a 400 error to the caller, and the footnote says KMS retries once any request that takes 250ms.
Claim drops the condition on re-encryption: the quote says existing data can be re-encrypted under new XKS keys only 'assuming the AWS service or your own application supports the action'.
Quote says requests are forwarded to a component in your network called an XKS Proxy; context says it forwards them to your key management infrastructure.
Quotes under the disable/block/delete question state the next API call fails for non-caching services, caching varies from 5 mins to 24 hrs, and in-use resources respond differently.
Quotes say automatic rotation is supported by the XKS specification, provided by most vendors, and occurs entirely in the external key manager.
Quote lists exactly the symmetric operations Encrypt, ReEncrypt, Decrypt and GenerateDataKey as supported by external keys.
Quote says XKS helps comply with rules or regulations requiring keys to be stored and used outside AWS under your control.
Quotes state KMS enforces policies you define and you can allow IAM users and roles from your account or other accounts to use and manage keys.
Quote supports 20,000 requests/month across all Regions and the context supports the exclusions, but the qualifier scope 'per account' is not stated in the quote or its context.
Quotes say GenerateDataKey encrypts a copy under the symmetric encryption KMS key you specify and returns both the plaintext copy and the encrypted copy.
Quotes state a grant can allow but not deny access, and context plus quote say an authorized principal can retire or revoke it, eliminating all permissions it allowed.
Quotes cover temporary use without policy changes, exactly one KMS key, cross-account keys and allow-not-deny; context names AWS principals and service principals.

Quote says propagation typically takes less than a few seconds and in some cases several minutes; the claim 'from a few seconds to several minutes' misstates the typical lower bound. Grant token part is supported.
Quote states grants allow only a subset of operations: view the key, use it in cryptographic operations, and create and retire grants.
Context and quote say integrated services commonly use grants; the service creates a grant on behalf of a user, uses it and retires it as soon as its task is complete.
The features-page context footnotes that FIPS 140-3 does not apply to AWS KMS in the China (Beijing) and China (Ningxia) Regions; the claim's 'all AWS KMS keys' drops this exception.
Quotes give least privilege on only needed keys, key ARN of each key in Resource, and wildcard Resource only for permissions that require it.
Quote states IAM allow has no effect without key policy permission, IAM deny works without it, and the default key policy enables IAM policies.
Quote says importing creates interoperable asymmetric and HMAC keys operating within and outside AWS; context states key material cannot be imported into custom key store keys.
Quote under the asymmetric and HMAC heading states permanent association, same material only, no automatic rotation, manual rotation possible.
Quote says imported material cannot be exported or returned in any form and you must keep a copy outside AWS, preferably in a key manager such as an HSM, to reimport.
Quotes and context state symmetric imported keys support on-demand rotation with multiple materials; current encrypts and decrypts, non-current only decrypt.
Quotes say you remain responsible for imported material and KMS does not maintain its durability at the same level as KMS-generated material.
Quote states integrated services use only symmetric encryption KMS keys and do not support encryption with asymmetric KMS keys.
Quotes under the console default key policy administrators statement match both parts of the claim.

Quote supports last successful operation with CloudTrail event ID per key; the qualifier condition (data key use outside KMS not tracked, do not rely on it alone before deletion) is not in the quote or context.
PutKeyPolicy Policy parameter shows minimum length 1, maximum 32768, and context states LimitExceededException when exceeded.
Quote states a KMS key policy does not automatically give permission to the account or its identities and needs an explicit statement for account administrators.
Quote and context state key policy is the resource policy and primary access control, exactly one per key, and IAM policies and grants can also control access.
Quote states IAM policies are global, key policies are Regional and control access only to a key in the same Region.
Quotes state all keys can be Enabled, Disabled, PendingDeletion; PendingImport only for imported material; Unavailable only for custom key store keys.
Key policy table row matches the three key types under the header with the same column order.
Logging table row gives CloudTrail trail or event data store for customer managed and AWS managed keys, not viewable for AWS owned keys.
